t: This bronze statue shows the painter John Everett Millais. It stands in John Islip Street, just north of Tate Britain, on a pedestal of Portland stone, and was designed by the sculptor Thomas Brock. Millais was a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and a child prodigy, who at eleven became the youngest student at the Royal Academy Schools. His painting Ophelia, from 1851 to 1852, embodies the group's historical and naturalist focus. Brock, who made this statue, is best known for the Victoria Memorial in front of Buckingham Palace, so the artist is in good company.
